summaries.summary: The slide defines 'ELASTICITY' as the ability of a body to recover its size and shape after deformation, citing McGraw-Hill, 2003. It emphasizes that resilient, only-purposeful behavior involves no 'advanced' behavior, relying on internal characteristics and resources to mask external forces, which is redundancy-based.
key_facts: ELASTICITY is defined as the ability of a body to recover its size and shape after deformation.
Resilient behavior is redundancy-based and does not involve 'advanced' behavior.
The system masks external forces using internal characteristics and resources.
visible_text: The ability of a body that has been subjected to an external force to recover its size and shape, following deformation
No 'advanced' behavior; system just makes use of its internal characteristics and resources so as to mask the action of external forces
